name: Ebstein Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Ebstein Anomaly

criteria.description: Apical displacement of the septal and posterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve by >8 mm/m² body surface area
Atrialization of a portion of the right ventricle due to abnormal tricuspid valve insertion
Presence of tricuspid valve regurgitation on Doppler echocardiography
Right atrial enlargement evident on imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets and atrialization of right ventricle confirmed by echocardiography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings; cardiac MRI may be used for further anatomical detail.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets

common.notes: Due to impaired right ventricular function

occasional.notes: Secondary to arrhythmias or low cardiac output

rare.notes: Due to paradoxical embolism via atrial septal defect

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas if cyanosis present
imaging: Echocardiography showing apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets and atrialized right ventricle
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical assessment
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and right atrial enlargement
genetic: No specific gene identified; sporadic cases predominate
other: Electrocardiogram showing right atrial enlargement, right bundle branch block, and pre-excitation patterns

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets
Fibrofatty replacement of right ventricular myocardium
Ventricular arrhythmias without tricuspid valve malformation

redFlags: Severe cyanosis in neonate or infant
references: Anderson RH, et al. Pediatric Cardiology. 4th ed. 2010.
Moss AJ, et al. The Clinical Recognition of Congenital Heart Disease. 2015.
